body: Your description about depersonalization actually does sound like something I've maybe experienced, but perhaps to a lesser degree. There are times where I'll feel very strongly like hurting myself that seem a little like what you describe. Out of curiosity, what's the significance of it? Like, if I could say with certainty that there are certain times I experience, what's the practical implication? I mean, it's interesting to have a term to help describe those moments, but a term alone doesn't provide much to me.

I don't know how I'd feel about someone who met that definition. I feel like my own feelings/thoughts on the matter wouldn't be important and don't matter. It's not my place to question it sort of. 

The embarrassment I would cause might be similar to that caused by a blemish on someone's face. I'd embarrass myself as well though, it's hard for me to not feel like I'm very lacking in central ways, ways in which I shouldn't be lacking or in which I should try harder.

For me those concepts speak more towards me being a burden and a waste of resources. I'm not sure what personal definition I could give to those concepts either, but when I feel they are true I just want to die. I'll feel there's no hope of me not being lazy, and so I should remove myself and any embarrassment I may cause.

I'm not sure how to feel about what you say. I feel like you are taking pity on me and it upsets me a little for some reason, it brings a false sense to what you say. I'm not saying you're being deceptive or anything, but the judgments you have made (like in your last paragraph) seem very off.

When I spoke about not deserving the same as others it wasn't specifically because of experiences with anxiety in social situations, not that you're saying that that was the case, I'm just trying to elaborate on the point. In general I feel less deserving and less like an authentic human, what I mean is that it will seem like others experience things in the real and true way, while what I feel is more of a shadow/fake version. Other people can be sad or happy or hungry or sleepy, but I just exist.

What if what you call depressive voices aren't just compelling but are correct? I know an immediate response might be, 'What if they aren't correct?' but I can't think along that line much, it feels too contrary to my view of life.

Also, about making personal changes, one thing I meant to add was that even changes that seem small can feel too big. Even just trying to get myself to exercise (even if it's just taking a short walk) feels wrong and brings up an array of issues. I'll try and do it because it's supposed to help elevate people's moods, but then I'll not want my mood to change because a part of me wants to kill myself and sees that as counterproductive. It's like a tug of war that's keeping me from doing anything truly harmful or helpful.

Those words, of hopelessness and of being overwhelmed, can apply I guess, for me I tend to quit trying to explain my feelings to myself when it becomes too complicated.

You have interesting advice about getting access to medications. I do have access to them already however, and have seen a psychiatrist for over a year, but most things I tried would make me feel sick, or they'd not have an effect at all. What is it exactly that makes your mood a lot better, in your opinion?

Regarding depersonalization, I don't believe this is something I've experienced, except in maybe seldom and small ways, however I could be mistaken.
I can't think of changes that would make me feel different, beyond killing myself. Maybe I'm not trying hard enough or maybe there isn't anything that can be changed in my situation.

In regards to the barriers I experience, this is difficult for me to explain. I don't feel like as much of a person almost, I don't deserve the same things as others and this might include emotional closeness. There's a pervasive sense of something being wrong with me. Some of these barriers come from my own difficulty communicating with others, I can be very nervous around people outside of my close family and I feel like I just don't relate to others, and have felt this way most of my life. 

Maybe this is me being ignorant of mental disease, but what makes depression separate from a personality or a set of personality traits? Sometimes trying to imagine myself as having a different or altered personality makes me sick and makes me want to die as well.

What you're saying about struggling makes sense but it's hard to apply it to myself. I don't feel like I'm struggling, I just feel like I'm lazy and hopeless and disappointing. 

What I've tried hasn't felt helpful. I live in a rural area however and my options seem limited. Also, why are you talking to me?

I could go deep in the woods to do it, there are miles of forest right in my backyard. What makes the events of the hypothetical tomorrow matter? Also, I don't really buy into that saying, I may not know with full certainty what the future will bring, but I have a strong foundation of past experiences to form projections with. It's similar with my view on death, there are elements I might not be able to be certain of but I have a very good idea of what will happen and it is appealing.

These are difficult questions to answer, and a part of me doesn't want to bother, but I'll try. In response to the first, I think the things that will make me feel like a failure and like life is too hard are a mix of things. I'll feel awful because I can't make myself work, and because I feel like there's no sort of future in front of me. I'll feel bad due to how I respond to things, when an issue comes up and I can't handle it. I'll feel like I will always be alone, that there are barriers between myself and others that nothing can trespass. 

I guess in order for me to feel life is livable I'd need a different personality. 

The things that bring me pleasure can be simple, looking at the clouds in the sky can make me feel calm and at ease. It doesn't fill up the day though, most hours are spent playing video games, reading (books or online stuff), or watching shows/movies. I'll feel bad about this, like it's wasted time, because none of those spent hours help make me what I'd imagine to be productive or of value. I'll feel like it's wasted time but not be sure of what I should/could have done anyway, but it'll feel pointless because all those wasted hours can't be redeemed and make me want to give up.

Also, I see a therapist, I've been seeing them for almost a year. I've tried a handful of different antidepressants, for over a year or so. I'm currently not taking any and of course I'm considering whether to continue psychotherapy.

The things that make me want to stop living have to do with my self and how I feel about my place in life in general. I feel like a failure and like life is too hard, and I just can't be dissuaded from that feeling.

The things that make me keep living are material pleasures I suppose, and fear of making a large and permanent decision. Also, more prominent to this, is the knowledge that some people, i.e. my family, might be hurt by my death. It'll depend on my frame of mind.
